savoury = having a salty or spicy flavour rather than a sweet one
bland = with very little flavour
stale = no longer fresh, especially bread or biscuits
perishable = likely to go bad quickly if not kept cold
pungent = having a very strong smell or taste
tangy = having a sharp, pleasant taste, often of citrus or yoghurt
succulent = tender and full of juice
palatable = pleasant enough to eat or drink
unpalatable = unpleasant to eat; hard to accept
mouth-watering = looking or smelling so good that you want to eat it
appetising = making you want to eat because of how it looks or smells
rancid = smelling or tasting unpleasant because fat has gone bad
soggy = unpleasantly wet and soft
crunchy = firm and making a sharp sound when you bite
tender = soft and easy to cut or chew
tough = difficult to chew because the meat is hard
lean meat = meat with little fat
wholesome = good for your health; made from simple, decent ingredients
nutritious = containing substances the body needs to stay healthy
moreish = so pleasant that you want another mouthful
